title: Bram and the Wolf
premise: Rafael Underhill, a mercenary whose god went silent years ago, keeps ledgers for the Guild of Impossible Things — until prayers start being answered again and her own forgotten vows come due. Guided by Bram, a wolf-shaped memory of someone she once loved, she must cross a country that was erased from every map, trading pieces of her past for passage. At the border of the vanished land, she learns the silent god never left; it became the winter itself, holding the country in stasis to keep its people from dying twice. To open the door out, Rafael must choose between restoring her memories and freeing the country — and she gives up Bram, the last warm thing she owns, so that spring can finally arrive.
about_author: Jonah Whitlock is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the personal effects of unclaimed estates. They write fantasy about people who keep records of things everyone else has agreed to forget.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: In Rafael's POV, we meet the Guild of Impossible Things through its accounts: bottled lullabies, second chances sold at discount. When a prayer is answered aloud in the guildhall — the first in years — the ledger pages begin rewriting themselves with debts in Rafael's name. Emotional beat: unease blooming into dread as her ordered world starts lying to her.

chapters.title: What the Wolf Remembers
chapters.summary: A wolf appears at the guild's door and only Rafael can see it; it speaks with the voice of Bram, a comrade she cannot remember losing. Following it, she finds the erased country on no map but hers, its borders humming like a struck bell. Emotional beat: longing and suspicion intertwined — she needs the wolf's guidance but cannot trust what it wants.

chapters.title: The Country That Was Not
chapters.summary: Inside the frozen nation, villages stand mid-gesture under unmelting snow, and the silent god speaks at last: it swallowed the country's death to spare its people, and Rafael's old vows helped seal it. The door out demands a memory of equal weight. Climax: Rafael realizes Bram is not a guide but the price already paid — her own memory, walking beside her.

chapters.title: Spring Owes No One
chapters.summary: At the threshold, Rafael must choose: keep Bram and let the winter hold forever, or release him and let the country die honestly and live again. She lets him go; snow becomes rain, the erased return to their names, and her ledger closes with one final entry written in her own hand. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into belonging — she walks out of a country that now exists, carrying nothing but spring.
